category.title: Machine Learning and Adaptive Decision Methods
category.proposed_overview: Machine learning studies prediction, representation, generation and sequential decision procedures under explicit mathematical and statistical models. This track begins with risk, complexity and generalization, then develops linear and kernel methods, trees, graphs, privacy and distributed training. Neural architectures, differentiation and optimization are followed by interpolation, representation learning, generative modeling and uncertainty. Online learning, bandits and reinforcement learning connect prediction to adaptive data collection and control. Further modules cover scalable kernel computation, implicit learning layers, efficient exact attention, low-rank adaptation, preference optimization, masked diffusion, risk calibration, verifiable generation, active querying and semi-supervised propagation. Each algorithm specifies its admissible inputs, outputs, branches and stopping rules. Its correctness, numerical behavior and statistical guarantees are separate results with explicit assumptions. Existing statistics, Bayesian computation and numerical-analysis suppliers are reused rather than duplicated. General transport, diffusion, Wasserstein-flow and random-matrix prerequisites precede their consumers. Examples and counterexamples illustrate boundaries and never supply other pages.
